originalSteps.title: Prepare unit-aware anchored camera space
originalSteps.goal: Keep scene coordinates precise while expressing the camera projection in physical metres.
originalSteps.trace: Scene coordinate − scene anchor → physical metres → camera view → clip coordinate
originalSteps.question: Why subtract the anchor before converting the position to f32?
originalSteps.answer: Narrowing a large coordinate first can erase a small displacement permanently. Subtracting in double precision keeps the local displacement available to the GPU.
originalSteps.result: The camera prepares equivalent mm/metre and anchor-relative projections without changing document ownership.
originalSteps.experiment: Run Fit, Pan Right, Fit, View Perspective and View Orthographic, and verify that navigation and original picking still work. In the typed code, compare physically equivalent mm/metre camera inputs and predict a distant anchor-relative fractional displacement. GPU anchor adoption follows later.
originalSteps.production: Explicit unit conversion and anchored camera projection are prepared. Shared GPU rebasing and reversed depth across all consumers remain required.
originalSteps.story: The document owns its coordinates and file unit. Convert scene distances to metres only while building the camera matrix. For a distant drawing, subtract the shared scene anchor in double precision before multiplying by the unit scale. Multiplying all clip components by one nonzero factor leaves their divided coordinates unchanged. Divide the perspective matrix by the unit scale so inverse consumers keep their numeric range. CPU rays invert around the precise target, form their direction locally and restore the world origin afterward. The ordinary matrix uses a zero anchor; later GPU consumers will adopt the same anchor together. Depth remains forward at this checkpoint.

originalSteps.title: Share one camera and measurement unit
originalSteps.goal: Use one scene unit for projection and measurement labels.
originalSteps.trace: camera.unit → physical projection scale and measurement suffix
originalSteps.question: What happens if measurement keeps an independent unit field?
originalSteps.answer: Projection and labels can disagree about the same scene. One camera-owned value gives them a shared interpretation without changing document coordinates.
originalSteps.result: The camera owns the scene unit used by projection and measurements.
